newsitem.title: CHINA: China punishes two more firms for illegal deals.
newsitem.headline: China punishes two more firms for illegal deals.

text.p: Two more of China's leading financial institutions, Haitong Securities and the Shenzhen Development Bank, have been punished for illegal stock transactions, the Shanghai Securities News said on Wednesday.
The newspaper said the two had illegally provided funds through overdrafts to clients for stock trading.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) has given them a warning and fined them five percent of the sums involved in the illegal transactions, the newspaper said.
It said Haitong's Beijing branch gave clients overdrafts of at least 9.1 million yuan while Shenzhen Development Bank's Beijing branch extended overdrafts of at least 10.9 million yuan.
Both companies will undergo a one-month reorganisation, the conclusions of which will be subject to checks and approvals by the CSRC, the newspaper said.

"China's securities markets are currently in a development phase and firmly seeking out and punishing all forms of trading based on overdrafts is necessary to ensure the healthy development of the markets," the paper quoted the CSRC as saying.
Late last week, the CSRC announced punishments for more than a dozen banks and securities houses for irregularities on the stock market.
